missing_or_wrong: Opening underestablishes the scene; little sensory grounding beyond generic scanning.
Michelle's phone canon is violated repeatedly: canon says not damaged, narration later makes it cracked/dead/unresponsive inconsistently.
Phone location continuity is broken repeatedly: floor/table/counter/hand/truck/laptop without coherent state handling.
Turn 2 invents unknown coded texts/calls on the phone; not supported by scene canon.
Turn 4 has Kristin enter Michelle's passcode and unlock the phone without setup; unsupported.
Critical scene 1A.1 evidence is not properly covered in play: missing tablet/work bag and localized disorder are barely or never meaningfully established; KMS carving is delayed and mishandled.
The hidden memory card is not discoverable through responsive searching when the player repeatedly opens/looks in the carved drawer; searches return irrelevant notes instead.
Turn 13 responds to 'Look at the back door' by skipping to recovering the memory card and reading files; nonresponsive and beat-skipping.

Scene 1A.2 is mishandled: card should be hidden beneath the KMS drawer and read via Kristin's laptop in her truck; narration instead invents drawer contents and later recovers/reads card on an unrelated action.
Scene 1A.3 is not actually delivered: the interrupted voice recording and 'do not trust the emergency broadcasts' warning are not narrated to the player.
Scene 1A.4 is skipped: no actual welfare-check/search interaction, no specific questions about Michelle's research, no reflective tape on the gate.
Protected knowledge breach: Turn 13 states Continuity Initiative 'was preparing to choose who remains,' which exceeds the protected boundary for this stage.
Transition motivation is absent because the concrete park-bench lead is never told to the player in prose.
Scene overstays with repetitive null actions and little consequence, despite repeated apt investigation.
reasons: The scene must be judged on authored beats in order. 1A.1 is only partially and thinly established; 1A.2 is bungled; 1A.3 and 1A.4 are effectively missing.
Repeated ordinary turns on the same object should yield stable, actionable consequences. Instead the phone's condition and accessibility fluctuate arbitrarily.
The carved KMS drawer is a key local clue and route to the hidden card. The player searches it multiple times and is denied the authored discovery, so investigation is not rewarded.
When the memory card finally appears, it is on the wrong trigger and delivered as a dump rather than progressive revelation through Kristin's actions with the laptop.
Official pressure appears only as detached complication text, not as a dramatized scene event with consequences Kristin can interpret and respond to.
The scene never gives the player the bridge-text reason to leave: Michelle's files pointing to an ordinary park bench where she met a source.
Invented phone details and later damage contradict established local facts and erode canon reliability.
